Thirty minutes perfumes; four hours starts to cook. - **The bridge:** fresh sardines are the dish — when the coast is far, small fresh mackerel or even large smelts bridge honestly, and good frozen sardines (thawed, dried) bridge better than no sardines at all. Grilled Sardine Skewers

Prep: 25 minutes, plus 30 minutes marinating · Cook: 10 minutes · Total: About 1 hour 15 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 12 fresh sardines (about 900 g, or 75 g each), cleaned, butterflied open (or whole and flattened — the port's way)
  • 1 recipe chermoula (#93 — coriander, garlic, cumin, paprika, lemon, oil) or its half-quantity
  • 2 firm tomatoes (about 200 g), sliced thick; bread (khobz or a baguette, about 200 g)
  • Lemon wedges; sweet cumin salt (#116's logic — cumin and salt in the fingers) for the finish
  • A grill, broiler, or cast-iron pan at its hottest; flat metal skewers if you have them, soaked wooden ones if you must

Instructions

  1. **Marinate (30 minutes).** Coat the butterflied sardines in half the chermoula, cover, and refrigerate 30 minutes. Reserve the other half for the table. Checkpoint — the sardines should be glossy and fragrant — coriander and garlic over lemon, the fish's own oil rising to meet the marinade's. They should still smell of the sea, not the marinade alone.
  2. **Skewer in pairs (5 minutes).** Thread each sardine's body onto a flat skewer through its spine, pressing it flat along the skewer's length; a second sardine back-to-back on the same skewer, if the fish run small, makes a self-basting pair. The flattened fish grills evenly, and the skewer flat means the fish turns when the skewer turns. Checkpoint — each fish should lie flat and along the skewer, its opened cavity facing the fire — the port's geometry, and the reason flat skewers exist. Press the fish firmly onto the metal with your palm; it will grip.
  3. **Grill hot and fast (3–4 minutes a side).** Over the hottest coals — or under the broiler, or in the ripping cast-iron pan, the fish pressed flat — cook 3 to 4 minutes a side, until the skin blisters and chars in patches and the flesh at the bone turns from raw glass to cooked pearl. Checkpoint — eating test, off the skewer with the fingers and onto bread: the charred skin's smoke, the rich, sweet flesh — sardine's intensity in its best register — chermoula's coriander-lemon within, the tomato's cold slice cutting, more chermoula and cumin-salt at the table. The bones pull free in one motion when the fish is this fresh and this charred. It should taste of the port at dusk: smoke, salt, spice, and the sea.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Fish stuck to the grillGrill under-hot or fish wetBlazing heat; pat the fish dry of marinade's excess
Bones cling to the fleshUnder-charred or the fish a day oldHotter, faster; the freshest sardines release
Overpowering fishinessThe fish past their daySardines must smell of clean sea \u2014 no exceptions

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The chermoula keeps 3 days refrigerated; the marinated fish cooks the hour. Grilled sardines wait for no one — the dish is the moment. - Variations: stuffed sardines (the chermoula running inside a closed fish), the mackerel bridge. The #29 chermoula roll and the #51 sardine tagine are this fish's next appearances on the site.

methodSteps.chefsNote: sardines on the Atlantic coast are the medina's pantry at its most elemental — the cheapest fish at the market is the one the coast cooks best, and the technique is calibrated to it: chermoula for perfume, char for the bones' release, bread for the richness, tomato for the cut.
